defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: replace(obj, obj) raises ValueError because the guard removes obj before the search
guard removes new_m from every traversed list, changing nesting level across groups
list.remove only drops the first occurrence; duplicates can survive
pre-existing: add() dedups only at top level, allowing nested duplicates
missing test for replace(obj, obj) self-replacement
votes.evidence_quote: `replace(obj, obj)` raises `ValueError`. The guard on line 37–38 removes `obj` from the list before the search loop at line 42 finds it, leaving nothing to match.
votes.justification: The first finding names the exact defect: self-replacement raises ValueError. It gives the right cause (the dedup guard removes the object before the search) and points at the dedup lines in src/scene.py.
